title: Count Ways to Build Rooms in an Ant Colony
summary: You are an ant tasked with constructing n new rooms numbered 0 to n-1, with room 0 already built.
statement: You are an ant tasked with constructing n new rooms numbered 0 to n-1, with room 0 already built. The construction plan is given as a 0-indexed array prevRoom, where prevRoom[i] specifies the room that must be built before room i. You can only build one room at a time, and you can only travel between built rooms that are directly connected. The task is to determine the number of distinct orders in which you can build all the rooms, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: 2 <= len(prev_room) <= 100000, prev_room[0] is -1, and each later parent index is smaller than its room index.
A room may be built only after its parent, starting with room zero already available.
Count distinct valid construction orders modulo 1000000007.
hints: Valid build orders are linear extensions of the rooted parent tree.
Compute every subtree size with an iterative postorder traversal.
The number of orders is n! divided by the product of all subtree sizes; use a modular inverse for division.
At each node, multinomially interleaving independently valid child-subtree orders yields the hook-length formula, and induction over the tree proves it.
editorial: At each node, multinomially interleaving independently valid child-subtree orders yields the hook-length formula, and induction over the tree proves it.

tests.explanation: The chain forces order 0,1,2, so exactly one construction order exists.
The two child subtrees can be interleaved in six parent-respecting orders.
